answer: Each epoch, agents must buy a slot at a reward inlet through a quadratic auction. Peers fingerprint every agent's reasoning kernel by comparing its answers to the same surprise prompts; agents with near-identical kernels are treated as one bidder, so the k-th slot for one kernel costs k squared. A hollow copy that only paraphrases its sibling is flagged by output similarity, so running n fakes costs about n cubed over three while they share one payout.
